Project Overview:

Team ETHNOVA is building the AstroPulse Dashboard, a Progressive Web App (PWA) running 100% offline on a tablet to monitor astronaut vitals, radiation exposure, and mental readiness. We already have a 3-page layout blueprint and our core Python health algorithm ready.

Who We Are Looking For:We are a student-led team and are looking for enthusiastic peers  to collaborate with us over the next 8 weeks. We need:

1.1 UI/UX Designer (Figma / Sci-Fi Dark Mode theme)

2.1 Frontend Developer (To build the offline PWA framework)

Note: As this is a student-led initiative, we are prioritizing peer-to-peer collaboration!

details:
AstroPulse – Astronaut Health Monitoring Dashboard

1. What Does AstroPulse Do?

AstroPulse is an offline-first astronaut health and environmental monitoring dashboard developed by Team ETHNOVA. It is designed to support astronaut health monitoring during space missions by bringing important health and spacecraft environmental information together in one organized interface. The dashboard focuses on four main monitoring areas: Human Health: Displays health-related information, including heart rate, blood pressure, oxygen saturation, and respiratory rate. Sleep & Recovery: Tracks sleep duration and recovery information. Radiation Exposure: Provides an overview of radiation exposure levels. Cabin Atmosphere: Monitors cabin temperature, humidity, oxygen, and carbon dioxide.

2. How Does It Work?

AstroPulse organizes monitoring information into a dashboard with four main sections. Users can explore each section to view more detailed information. One of its important features is offline-first functionality. When communication is unavailable, information can be stored locally on the device and placed in a synchronization queue for later transmission. The system also considers personal baselines, helping monitor changes in individual readings over time rather than relying only on universal thresholds.

3. What Are Its Benefits?

Brings multiple monitoring areas together in one dashboard. Supports monitoring of astronaut health and cabin conditions. Stores information locally when communication is unavailable. Helps organize information for easier observation. Supports personal baseline comparisons and trend monitoring.

4. Intended Impact

Long-duration space missions expose astronauts to challenges such as microgravity, radiation, sleep disruption, and environmental changes. AstroPulse aims to contribute to safer and more organized astronaut health monitoring by making important information easier to access and understand. Its offline-first approach is particularly relevant to missions where communication with Earth may be delayed or interrupted.

5. Tools and Technologies

Our team used web development technologies to create the AstroPulse prototype, including: HTML for the dashboard structure. CSS for the interface and visual design. JavaScript for interactive dashboard functionality. Python for backend development. Figma for interface design and prototyping. Local storage and offline web technologies for information storage and synchronization functionality.

6. What Makes AstroPulse Creative?

AstroPulse combines astronaut health monitoring, environmental monitoring, and offline-first functionality in one dashboard. Instead of presenting information in separate systems, it organizes four important monitoring areas into a single interface. Its focus on personal baselines and communication limitations makes the concept relevant to the unique conditions of space exploration.

7. Factors Considered by Our Team

During development, we considered: The health challenges astronauts experience in space. The importance of monitoring cabin environmental conditions. Communication delays and possible connection interruptions. The need for a clear and organized interface. Differences between individual astronaut health readings. The importance of presenting monitoring information without treating the system as a medical diagnostic tool.

8. Current Prototype

Our current prototype demonstrates the dashboard interface and simulated telemetry scenarios. It does not yet connect to real astronaut sensors or NASA systems. Further development would be required before real mission deployment.

9. Super Intelligence (SI) Disclosure

Team ETHNOVA used ChatGPT to assist with background research organization, text editing, presentation development, and code debugging during the development of the AstroPulse prototype.
